scope: Theorem 1.1 (Initialized computation by a solenoidal force) of the manuscript “Finite Instructions and Solenoidal Shear Flows” (preprints/Finite-Instructions-and-Solenoidal-Shear-Flows-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0cdc2abd5b1a3d15), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a positive computable viscosity ν on the unit flat torus T3. There is an algorithm taking a deterministic one-tape machine M with head moves in {−1, 0, 1} and a finite input word w to an effective smooth force fM,w with these properties. (i) The force is divergence free and has zero spatial mean. Equation (1) has a global smooth solution (u, p) = (U, 0), unique in the classical class just specified on every finite time interval. (ii) All mixed derivatives of U and fM,w are globally bounded, and the kinetic energy is uniformly bounded. Both fields have period one for t ≥ 1 and vanish on a neighborhood of every integer time. The period-one mechanism after initialization depends on M alone. (iii) With fixed label a∗ = (1/8, 3/8, 1/2) and fixed open strip O = {(x, y, z) : 1/2 < x < 1}, the trajectory enters O at a finite time if and only if M halts on w, including an initially halted machine. For arbitrary fixed real ν > 0, the same formulas and conclusions hold; the evaluation algorithm is then relative to that parameter.
